title: Vibe Coding with Confidence — Itamar Friedman, Qodo
talk_summary: Itamar Friedman of Qodo argues that 'vibe coding with confidence' requires moving from chat/IDE autocomplete to CLI-driven, composable agent workflows that span the whole SDLC (plan, code, test, review) with high-quality review and testing as first-class 'red team' steps. He demos a CLI that can generate specialized agents (e.g., a review agent) and pipe agents together, and speculates about A2A communication and swarms of specialized agents.

takeaways.technique: Composable CLI agent pipelines (pipe agent outputs into next agent)
takeaways.what_they_do: They chain specialized agents via shell-style piping: a code-gen agent's output feeds a coverage agent, whose output feeds a review agent, rather than one monolithic agent doing everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I want to run code of code generating code and then I want to run the cover ... and then I want a review agent

takeaways.technique: Agent-generated specialized agents with explicit output schemas and success criteria
takeaways.what_they_do: A meta-agent creates a new specialized agent (e.g., 'merge review agent') with instructions, tool list, an output schema, and explicit success/failure criteria so the caller can judge whether the run succeeded.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can also tell it to have some success or or or failure criteria to know that something happen well or not

takeaways.technique: Shift review/testing left as 'red team' with org best practices injected
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat review and testing as a red-team function that runs with accumulated organizational best practices as context, and push it earlier (pre-commit) rather than only post-push.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the code review tool collects best practices over time and this the context that is coming from the codto aware

takeaways.technique: CLI as universal interface for agents (logs, piping, background runs)
takeaways.what_they_do: They expose agents as CLI commands so they can be run in background, piped, logged to files, and hooked into pre/post-commit, rather than locked inside an IDE plugin.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can tell it dump all the logs somewhere ... How do you do that with an ID plugin? You can, but you need to hack it

takeaways.technique: A2A / agent discoverability for parallel specialized agents
takeaways.what_they_do: He speculates about a 'command line for A2A' so many specialized agents with different credentials and best practices can run in parallel and hand off work with discoverability/handshakes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: who is using A2A no one is using it so it's still way to go
